brief.desc: Bearish, score 18. Forced selling into a Fed hiking cycle took GLD 3.67% lower to a new 52-week low on twice the previous day's volume. Confidence in the trend is high, but the market is stretched enough that a bounce from here would not change the call.
brief.yr: GLD closed at 322.87, down 3.67%, on a 320.95 to 328.60 range near the low, ending the week down 9.17%. Volume was 23.18M shares against 11.35M the day before, which looks like liquidation. Same-day headlines blamed Fed hike bets and an AI-led equity rout. Gold fell even as bond yields reportedly dropped, so the haven bid failed and gold was sold for cash.
brief.to: Base case (50%) is a grind toward 300 in GLD as the December hike is confirmed and equity stress forces more sales. A relief bounce to 335-345 has 35% odds and a reversal to 360 or higher 15%. Thanksgiving closes US markets on Nov 26, and no 2026 data calendar was verified this run, so check PCE, GDP and FOMC dates before relying on them. Watch whether Friday's 320.95 low holds on Monday. This view flips bullish if the 10-year TIPS real yield closes below 2.60%.

brief.why: The Fed is hiking, not cutting. On Nov 18 New York Fed President Williams said the Fed would likely need to raise rates again, Musalem said several more hikes may be needed, and markets priced a 97.8% chance of a December hike (NST citing CME FedWatch). The 10-year real yield rose from 2.60% on Nov 5 to 2.92% on Nov 16 before easing to 2.88%, while breakevens fell to 2.16%. The market is endorsing the hawkish path, so gold has neither a real-rate argument nor an inflation-hedge argument. The dollar, near a 19-month high, passes each leg up in rate expectations straight through to gold. Friday added a second mechanism: the AI-led equity rout should have helped gold as a haven, but investors meeting margin calls sold what was liquid and still in profit. The last CFTC print, as of Oct 20, showed managed money net long 104,206 contracts. If that book is still largely in place, every equity drawdown becomes a gold sale. No central-bank or ETF buying was verified this run, and GLD's doubled volume points to selling, not accumulation.
brief.cons: Worst week since March is the headline everywhere, and a near-certain December hike is being repeated, so bearishness is now consensus and this call shares it. GLD is 13.88% below its 50-day average and 0.6% above its 52-week low after a 9.17% week, which is stretched. With a hike almost fully priced, the next Fed surprise is more likely dovish than hawkish. The trend call is right, but shorting at a 52-week low after a volume spike is the late trade. A sharp, short relief rally inside a downtrend is the likeliest path. The positioning data is a month old, so nobody knows how much long book remains.
fals: Soften: GLD closes back above 335.18, the Nov 19 close, by the Nov 25 close, meaning Friday's breakdown failed; the score moves toward 35.
Invert: the 10-year TIPS real yield (FRED DFII10) closes below 2.60%, the Nov 5 low, within the next two weeks; that flips the view bullish.

Weak joint: the liquidation thesis assumes specs are still heavily long, but the latest CFTC data is as of Oct 20 and no ETF-flow or central-bank figure was read; if positioning is already flat the downside fuel is gone. Check the next CFTC release and GLD holdings on Monday.
